subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards remain full-content-only, add an explicit append/delta mode for affected deployments, or require a different coalescing/backpressure design before the linked pull request can land?
rationale: Current code follows the full-content direction adopted to prevent truncation, but live users now report severe latency and the current linked cadence mitigation may not be enough; adding an append mode would add config and compatibility surface.

options.title: Require Proven Opt-In Append Mode
options.body: Keep full-content updates as the default, but allow a documented append/delta mode only with live proof that affected deployments keep complete final content and recover latency.

options.title: Stay Full-Content Only
options.body: Reject append-mode config and require a stronger full-content coalescing/backpressure fix with live Feishu timing proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Accept Current Coalescing Candidate
options.body: Proceed with the linked coalescing pull request after conflicts and proof gaps are resolved, accepting that some reported deployments may still need follow-up.

recommendation.title: Require Proven Opt-In Append Mode
recommendation.body: Keep full-content updates as the default, but allow a documented append/delta mode only with live proof that affected deployments keep complete final content and recover latency.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the Feishu plugin community maintainer, and the decision is specific to Feishu channel behavior and config.
